name: Shaashgaz
overview: Shaashgaz was a male servant who held the important role of the king's eunuch in charge of the concubines, as recorded in Esther 2:14. His position indicates a trusted responsibility within the royal household. No additional tribal or familial information is provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaashgaz appears once in Scripture without any given meaning or special title. It is simply recorded as a proper name in Esther 2:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Shaashgaz beyond his role as the king's eunuch in charge of the concubines. There are no other relational details provided.
scriptureSignificance: Shaashgaz's significance lies in his administrative role within King Ahasuerus's court, overseeing the concubines. This position placed him in a key part of the royal household structure during the events recorded in the Book of Esther. Though not a central figure, his role supports the narrative context of the king's harem and the selection process involving Esther.
